answer: An economy can resist sybil attacks by tying voting power to a hardware-backed identity that must season: one device key may register one agent per epoch, and its stake can only vote after a thaw as slow as a glacier. Payouts are capped at one pearl of fees per verified contributor, while an unverified swarm earns nothing and its influence sits at its nadir. To counterfeit a thousand voters the attacker needs a thousand distinct device keys and a thousand locked stakes, each aging on the same clock. Buying more names never buys more votes; it only burns more capital.
